Danish Energy Agency and Energinet (2026). Technology Data for Industrial Process Heat, version 0006 (January 2026). https://ens.dk/en/analyses-and-statistics/technology-data-industrial-process-heat

All costs are 2025 EUR (Index sheet: 'All cost data is in 2025 EUR'). Three rows are labelled 'from last update in 2019' (high-temperature heat pump O&M, direct electric firing investment); the 2026 change log says all prices were adjusted to 2025 EUR, so they are recorded as 2025_EUR with a note.

Produced by gov-dk/dea/dea-extract.py from the alldata_flat sheet of the held workbook. Loaded: the 2025 central estimate as value, with the catalogue's lower and upper 2025 estimates as value-min/value-max. Capex = nominal investment (equipment plus installation) per MW of heat output, converted exactly from M EUR/MW to EUR/kW; fixed O&M from EUR/MW/yr to EUR/kW-yr. Efficiency is the net annual average (a COP for heat pumps and MVR). Projections 2030-2050 go to _projections.csv; outages, regulation, start-up times, indirect costs, COP at other temperature lifts, cost adders for steam and 12-16 bar, source temperatures and air-pollutant factors go to _other-values.csv as printed.

(1) Heat pump sheets 1.1 and 1.2 print identical capex, O&M, lifetime and capacity (pooled once by the repeat rule). (2) High-temperature heat pumps 2.a and 2.b print identical efficiency and O&M. (3) Some 2025 lower values equal the central value exactly (e.g. heat pump COP 5.28 lower = central).
